caseno:
First Misc. Appeal No. 381 of 1980
With
Civil Revision No. 115 (F.M.) of 1980
lawyer:
K.A. Bakr with Mahbubur Rahman, Advocates ------ for appellants 
Mohammadullah, Advocate ------ for respondent No. 1
parties:
Jupitar Glass Industries Ltd. & Ors
Vs.
Titas Gas Transmission & Distribution Co. Ltd
full_judgment:
Md. Altaf Hossain, J:— This appeal is directed against an order dated 10-6-80 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dacca, in Title Suit No. 664 of 1979 of his rejecting plaintiffs' prayer for temporary injunction made in the Suit. The plaintiffs filed the suit for a declaration that the public notice issued by the defendants and published in the local dailes including the Bangladesh Observer on 16-6-79 is not valid, binding and enforceable against the plaintiffs and that the increase in the price of gas made in the aforesaid notification could not be made effective. The plaintiffs on the basis of several contracts with defendant No.1 became consumers of gas for running their industries. It was stipulated in the contracts that the current rate would be Tk. 9/- per 1000 cft. The contracts provided that in case the company would increase the rate it shall either by publication or by letter posted in the mails give 30 days' notice of the change of the price of gas. The consumers might elect to terminate the contract at the end of such period. But the defendant company has in contravention of the terms of the contract has, without giving 30 days notice as required, increased the rate of gas to Tk. 16/-per thousand cft and has issued the impugned public notice. Hence the plaintiffs filed the Suit. In the suit, the plaintiffs prayed for a temporary injunction on the allegations, inter alia, that if the plaintiffs were not granted the temporary injunction the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss inasmuch as their industries will be closed, good-will be destroyed, employees will be rendered unemployed giving rise to various litigations and causing serious inconveniences to the general public. Plaintiffs' prayer was opposed. The learned Subordinate Judge on hearing the parties and on consideration of their respective cases became of the view that the plaintiffs had no prima facie case and that plaintiffs' loss, if any, could be only pecuniary and rejected plaintiffs' prayer for temporary injunction. 

 2. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs have preferred this appeal. 

 3. Mr. K.A. Bakr, the learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiffs submits that the plaintiffs had a prima facie case and the learned Subordinate Judge has erred in law in taking the view that the plaintiffs had no prima facie case. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has also erred in taking the view that the plaintiffs could be compensated in money. 

 4. Mr. Mohammadullah, the learned Advocate for the respondent, on the other hand, has argued that the plaintiffs' have no prima facie case in as much as the gas price has been increased in pursuance of directive of the Government which was binding on the defendants as well as on the plaintiffs. He further submits that it is apparent that the loss complained of by the plaintiffs can be compensated in money. 

 6. It appears from this clause that change in the price of gas could be effected either by publication or letter giving 30 days notice. In the instant case, the price was changed with retrospective effect and 30 days notice has not been given. It can hardly be disputed that plaintiffs have a prima facie case for getting the declaration prayed for. We refrain from saying anything more at this stage lest this should prejudice any of the parties. The main question in this appeal is whether the plaintiffs will subtler irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-appellants have submitted that if the injunction is not granted industries will be closed, good-will of the plaintiffs' industries will be destroyed, the employees of the plaintiffs will be rendered unemployed, giving rise to litigations and serious inconveniences. These alleged con-sequences are evidently remote. The immediate in conveniences would be that the plaintiffs will require to get gas at the enhanced rate. In case he plaintiffs succeed in the suit, they will be at liberty to recover the excess amount paid by them. From this, it is evident that the loss that might occur to the plaintiffs is one which can be compensated in money. The learned Subordinate Judge after considering the cases of the respective parties have come to, the conclusion that the alleged injury was re-mote and may be compensated in money. We do not see any reason to take a different view and to interfere with this finding of the learned Subordinate Judge. 

 8. In the circumstances, though we find, disagreeing with the learned Subordinate Judge, that the plaintiffs have a prima facie case, we are of the opinion that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get a temporary injecting because the injury that the plaintiffs are likely to sustain can be compensated in money.
